---
title: "Detailed itineraries"
description: >
  The legs of each trip, with their times, distances, routes and
  geometries: the fastest trip, the alternatives, and the street edges a
  trip uses.
---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
source("setup.R")
```

`travel_time_matrix()` says how long a trip takes; `detailed_itineraries()`
says how it is made: each leg on foot, by bicycle, by car or on a ride,
with its duration, waiting time, distance, route and line.

Itineraries by public transport need timetables: on routes given only by
frequencies (such as the São Paulo sample that ships with the package) the
departures of a Monte Carlo draw are not trips that run, and public
transport is refused there. This page uses the Porto Alegre sample of r5r
2.5.0 (about 2 MB, downloaded once), whose bus and train feeds have
timetables.

```{r data, message = FALSE}
library(peabiru)
poa <- poa_sample(c("poa_osm.pbf", "poa_eptc.zip", "poa_trensurb.zip",
                    "poa_points_of_interest.csv"))
poa_network <- build_network(poa, n_threads = 2)
poi <- read.csv(file.path(poa, "poa_points_of_interest.csv"))
poi[, c("id", "lon", "lat")]
monday <- as.POSIXct("2019-05-13 14:00:00", tz = "America/Sao_Paulo")
```

## The fastest trip

By default (`shortest_path = TRUE`) each pair of origin and destination gets
the fastest trip leaving within `time_window` minutes of the departure time.
The origins and destinations are paired row by row; a single origin or
destination is repeated to match the other.

```{r fastest}
from <- poi[poi$id == "farrapos_station", ]
to <- poi[poi$id == "praia_de_belas_shopping_center", ]
trip <- detailed_itineraries(
  poa_network, from, to,
  mode = c("WALK", "TRANSIT"),
  departure_datetime = monday,
  n_threads = 2
)
trip[, c("option", "departure_time", "total_duration", "segment", "mode",
         "segment_duration", "wait", "distance", "route")]
```

The result is an `sf` data frame with one `LINESTRING` per leg, in WGS 84:

```{r map, fig.alt = "The legs of the trip, coloured by mode: a short walk, a train ride, a walk to the bus, a bus ride and a last walk."}
plot(trip["mode"], main = NULL, key.pos = 1, lwd = 3)
```

## Alternatives

With `shortest_path = FALSE` the trips are routed with R5's multi-criteria
router (McRAPTOR) over `time_window` departure times sampled in the window,
and each sequence of routes gives one option, the fastest of its kind.
`suboptimal_minutes` keeps the options up to that many minutes slower than
the best.

```{r alternatives}
options <- detailed_itineraries(
  poa_network, from, to,
  mode = c("WALK", "TRANSIT"),
  departure_datetime = monday,
  shortest_path = FALSE,
  suboptimal_minutes = 10,
  drop_geometry = TRUE,
  n_threads = 2
)
rides <- options[options$mode != "WALK", ]
summary_of_options <- options[options$segment == 1,
                              c("option", "departure_time", "total_duration")]
summary_of_options$routes <- tapply(rides$route, rides$option, paste,
                                    collapse = " > ")[as.character(summary_of_options$option)]
summary_of_options
```

The first option walks all the way; the others ride the train and a bus,
or two buses.

With a `fare_structure` each option also gets its fare (`total_fare`) and
the fare paid by the end of each leg (`cumulative_fare`); see the article
on [fares](fares.html).

## Street edges and stops

`osm_link_ids = TRUE` adds, for each street leg, the 'OpenStreetMap' way ids
and the indices of the street network's edges it goes along (the
`edge_index` of `street_network_to_sf()`), and for each ride the stops
where it boards and alights:

```{r ids}
ids <- detailed_itineraries(
  poa_network, from, to,
  mode = c("WALK", "TRANSIT"),
  departure_datetime = monday,
  osm_link_ids = TRUE,
  n_threads = 2
)
ids$osm_id_list <- substr(ids$osm_id_list, 1, 30)
sf::st_drop_geometry(ids)[, c("segment", "mode", "osm_id_list",
                              "board_stop_id", "alight_stop_id")]
```

## Every origin to every destination

`all_to_all = TRUE` routes from each origin to each destination instead of
row by row. `drop_geometry = TRUE` leaves the lines out and returns a
table without geometry, and `output_dir` writes one CSV file per pair instead of
returning the result.

```{r all}
places <- poi[1:3, ]
all <- detailed_itineraries(
  poa_network, places, places,
  mode = "WALK",
  all_to_all = TRUE,
  drop_geometry = TRUE,
  n_threads = 2
)
unique(all[, c("from_id", "to_id", "total_duration", "total_distance")])
```

## Trip options

To see every trip worth considering between two points, faster or cheaper, with fewer transfers or less walking, and not only the fastest one, see `trip_options()`, peabiru's own multi-criteria planner: [Trip options](trip-options.html).
